compareDisposition.rationale: No distinct two-source pairing adds more than this passage and its existing Scripture connections.

observations.body: A lawyer stands to test Jesus by asking what he must do to inherit eternal life. Jesus turns him to the law and asks how he reads it.
observations.label: A lawyer tests Jesus with a life question

observations.body: The passage presents Testing, asking, reading, answering, and doing as the scene's observable response or movement.
observations.label: Testing, asking, reading, answering, and doing

observations.body: The passage places Love of God and neighbor in the law beside Testing, asking, reading, answering, and doing.
observations.label: Love of God and neighbor in the law

payload.posture: Read Luke 10:25–28 as one movement in the temptation of Jesus, keeping the passage's actions, setting, sequence, and limits visible.
payload.tension: The passage states a lawyer stands to test Jesus by asking what he must do to inherit eternal life. Jesus turns him to the law and asks how he reads it. It does not by itself supply every cause or later interpretation of this part of the temptation of Jesus.
payload.title: A lawyer tests Jesus with a life question
